questions.q: What is the real difference between a core server and a read replica in Neo4j causal clustering?
options: Core servers hold the full graph and participate in Raft consensus and can become leader; read replicas hold an async copy, serve reads, and can never become leader
Core servers and read replicas are functionally identical, just named differently
Read replicas can accept writes but core servers cannot
Core servers only exist for backups, not for serving traffic
questions.explain: Core servers participate in the write-consensus tier; read replicas exist purely to scale read throughput and never join Raft consensus.

questions.q: Why do production Neo4j causal clusters typically run an odd number of core servers, such as three or five?
options: Raft consensus needs a majority to agree before a write or leader election is considered valid, and an odd count avoids tie votes
Neo4j licensing only permits odd numbers of core servers
It's an arbitrary convention with no technical reason
Even numbers of core servers cause data corruption
questions.explain: This is the same quorum-based reasoning behind avoiding even-numbered voting members in any consensus-driven cluster.

questions.q: What does 'causal consistency' actually guarantee to a client in a Neo4j causal cluster?
options: A client that writes data and then reads is guaranteed to see its own write, even if the read is routed to a different server
All clients see all writes from all other clients instantly, everywhere
Writes are guaranteed to never fail under any circumstances
Read replicas are guaranteed to always be perfectly in sync with core servers at every instant
questions.explain: The guarantee is specifically about a single client's own read-after-write consistency, enforced via bookmarks — not global instant consistency.

questions.q: How do Neo4j drivers enforce causal consistency across sessions?
options: By passing a bookmark from a write session into a subsequent read session, requiring the server has caught up to at least that point
By routing every read and write to the same single server permanently
By disabling read replicas entirely until the write has been confirmed
Causal consistency is not actually enforced by anything in the driver
questions.explain: Bookmarks represent how far the transaction log has progressed, and a session can require a server has reached at least that bookmark before running a query.

questions.q: A client wants to add ten read replicas to boost write throughput. What's wrong with this plan?
options: Read replicas only scale read throughput — they don't participate in Raft consensus and cannot accept writes, so adding more of them does nothing for write capacity
Nothing is wrong — adding read replicas is the correct way to scale writes in Neo4j
Read replicas actually reduce read throughput, so this makes things worse across the board
This is impossible because Neo4j clusters cannot have more than three read replicas total
questions.explain: Write capacity in a causal cluster is bound by the core server tier and Raft consensus, not by the number of read replicas.
